method: Complete XAML and code-behind source reading; code-behind reread without truncation; pinned Git blob identity verified.
findings: Value/Minimum/Maximum/Step dependency properties lack coercion or validation callbacks. Programmatic assignments and changed limits do not enforce a shared finite ordered range.
Empty text and ResetToZero assign zero without clamping Minimum. Increment clamps only upper bound; decrement clamps only lower bound. Negative or nonfinite Step is not explicitly rejected.

Numeric normalization replaces periods with commas but parses with current culture, then emits invariant culture for fractions. Whole-number path casts double to int despite default Maximum double.MaxValue; larger values lack checked conversion admission.

TextChanged normalization may return before Value assignment: when normalized text differs but formatted current text already matches, model remains unchanged on that branch. Exact UI reachability depends on culture, binding and input sequence.

Paste accepts character whitelist without enforcing one decimal separator; typed input uses a separate separator rule. PreviewKeyDown numeric whitelist excludes decimal keys despite PreviewTextInput allowing separators.
Caret positioning subtracts Suffix length although suffix is a separate overlaid TextBlock, not appended by UpdateTextFromValue.

Repeat timer stops on selected mouse-up/leave paths; no Unloaded or LostMouseCapture handler appears. Click and preview-down both adjust value; actual routed-event double adjustment needs WPF runtime reproduction.
limits: No WPF runtime execution or end-to-end delay-profile binding validation. Static source concerns are not proven defects in our Rust dedup library.
